l: The Special Operations and Investigations Bureau is responsible for the direction and coordination of the Tactical Command, and the Investigative and Support Command.

1. Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Section - responsible for responding to hostage situations, barricaded persons, sniper incidents, and other incidents which require the utilization of personnel specifically equipped and trained to function in support of the patrol operations division.
a. Crisis Negotiation Unit - respond to critical incidents for the purpose of negotiating the safe surrender of hostage takers or barricaded suspects and the safe release of hostages. TBP 8.03
b. Criminal Tracking Unit - provides uniformed support for Narcotics, Vice, Intel, Gang, SWAT and other units. The Unit targets, identifies and apprehends prolific offenders.
c. Tactical Medic - provides immediate medical care to injured or ill police officers or any civilians who require emergent or urgent medical attention during the course of the police mission.
a. Mounted Patrol Unit - provide specialized patrol on horseback to selected areas of the city, assistance in crowd control for special events, and may assist in searches for missing persons.
b. Dignitary Protection Detail - provide executive protection for the Mayor of the City of Fort Worth.

a. Narcotics - responsible for the investigation of all narcotic offenses and the execution of related search warrants. The Narcotics Section includes DEA Task Force, the HIDTA Task Force, and three (3) Complaint Teams.

(1) High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) - a federally funded multi-agency narcotic task force with enforcement responsibility at the organized crime level within an eleven (11) county area of North Texas. Responsible for the disruption of illicit drug trafficking, gathering and reporting intelligence data, and conducting undercover operations.

2. Vice Section - responsible for the detection and suppression of criminal activities including, but not limited to, gambling, prostitution, public lewdness, obscenity law violations, alcoholic beverage code, nuisance abatement, and any crimes against public morals.

a. K-9 Unit - features an officer paired with a specially trained dog to provide assistance to narcotics and field officers in building searches, locating missing persons, locating narcotics, and conducting specialized maneuvers.

(1) Interdiction Team - Canine handlers who are narcotics investigators with the mission of providing trained canine to assist in the detection of narcotics and for other such duties. Members of this unit may be assigned to the HIDTA Airport Group.

b. Criminal Investigative Unit (CIU) – detectives tasked with the responsibility of coordinating drug/vice offenses, communicating with Forensic Science personnel for lab analysis, monitoring prisoner detention and submitting of criminal cases to the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office.

c. Permits - maintains files relative to investigations, applications concerning city permits, permit applicants, and permit holders as appropriate. Conducts inspections to verify that permits are issued or retained appropriately. Participates in the protest function of permit or license issuance and renewals.

3. Gang Section - responsible for the detection, suppression and disruption of criminal street gang activity and successfully identifying, targeting and presenting for criminal prosecution those who are involved in illegal gang activity.
a. Electronic Surveillance Unit - provide technological support and electronic surveillance to departmental investigative sections and special events within the City of Fort Worth.

b. Operations and Surveillance Team (OST) - routinely research, surveil and apprehend Part 1/Prolific offenders engaging in organized crime and assist any member of the police department needing a covert component to their investigation.
c. Special Events/Emergency Response (SEER) and Community Emergency Response Teams (CERT)

(1). SEER provides department and officer compliance with the National Incident Management System (NIMS) certifications and training, and has primary responsibility for coordination of special and/or large-scale events as the designee for the Chief of Police, defined and outlined in the City of Fort Worth Outdoor Event Ordinance #19255-08-2010.
(2). C.E.R.T educates and organizes citizens about disaster preparedness for hazards that may impact their neighborhoods and educates citizens in basic disaster response skills.

a. Homeland Security Unit - provide the Chief of Police intelligence information regarding terrorist and subversive group threats to citizens, key resources, and venues in the City of Fort Worth; provide criminal intelligence to the department's investigative sections and special events occurring within the City; work jointly with the Fort Worth INTEX fusion center for research of information and intelligence; accept, research, store, and distribute Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) per DOJ guidelines; liaison with the FBI JTTF; and, provide and coordinate with respective agencies for the security of dignitaries visiting the City of Fort Worth. The Intelligence Exchange Section lieutenant shall be the department's Homeland Security liaison. TBP 8.10

b. Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) - designed to serve as the real-time information and intelligence hub of the Police Department by providing actionable intelligence to officers and investigators within the department in addition to assisting external law enforcement agencies in furtherance of ongoing criminal investigations.

c. Intelligence Analysis/Fusion Unit (IAU) – also known as the Fusion Unit, sworn and non-sworn analysts focusing on issues of homeland security, tactical intelligence and in-depth research of long-term strategic projects.

(1) Crime Stoppers Detail and Campus Crime Stoppers Detail - collect community-based information or school-related information from Crime Stoppers of Tarrant County, provide initial computer research and vetting in relation to the tips, and verify the information given by the tipster.

Air Support is under the supervision of a Lieutenant and is responsible for providing support to patrol ground units, aerial surveillance, and aerial preventative patrol for enhanced consistency in operations and deconfliction.

The Violent Crime Initiative (VCI) is a department-wide effort to combat and reduce violent crime in the city. The VCI is led by a Captain who is responsible for facilitating a meeting between enforcement units (i.e., Directed Response Units (DRU), Narcotics, Vice, etc.) and investigative units (i.e., Gun Violence, Homicide, Robbery, etc.) and the six (6) patrol bureau representatives to discuss and review ideas to address violent crime.

1. Crime Analysts, which are non-sworn analysts focusing on crime statistics and identifying emerging crime trends for both the Patrol Divisions and the Violent Crime Initiative, are assigned to the Violent Crime Initiative to enhance consistency in operations and deconfliction.
A. The Criminal Investigations Division is responsible for technical support, follow-up investigation, and case filing for all offenses investigated by the following sections:
a. Homicide Unit - investigate murders, suicides, and incident reports concerning deceased persons.
(1) Cold Case Detail - review, analyze, and prioritize unsolved cases for potential leads for follow-up investigation.
b. Robbery Unit - investigate all robbery offenses, to include financial institution and armored vehicle robberies.

c. Major Case Unit - investigate Critical Police Incidents as outlined in General Order 356.00; murder for hire; active kidnapping; offenses designated as “Hate Crimes,” fraud cases of $150,000 or more, and special investigations/assignments as directed by the chain of command.

(1) Missing Persons Detail - investigate all missing and runaway juveniles and the investigation of all adults who are missing under suspicious circumstances. d.Fugitive Unit - assignment of probable cause arrest warrants generated by members of the department and the service of these warrants; assist other agencies with arrests within the city to include teletype warrants from other agencies; assist other agencies with apprehension of fugitives on collateral requests generated through the U.S. Marshal Services; and, transportation of persons arrested by other agencies on our warrant.

e. Gun Violence Investigation Team – respond to all shooting calls involving someone who has been shot or, if there are no injuries, there is a known suspect or a suspect in custody. Investigators will not respond to shootings where there is only property damage.
a. Domestic Violence Unit - investigate domestic violence threats, assaults, retaliations, protective order violations, other family-related offenses, and stalking.
b. Crimes Against Children Unit/Internet Crimes Against Children

(1) Crimes Against Children (CACU) - responsible for thoroughly investigating all reported offense involving physical and sexual abuse of children; investigating all fatalities of a child five (5) years of age or under where death is likely from apparent Sudden Unexplained Infant Death (SUID) of an infant due to natural or unnatural causes; death caused by a parent, family member, or caregiver involving abuse or neglect; any accidental death to include drowning, suffocation, or drug or alcohol overdose; and apparent natural unattended death.
(2) Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) – investigates all technology-facilitated abuse and sexual exploitation of children involving the Internet.

c. Human Trafficking Unit - identify and recover victims of human trafficking. Investigate all Human Trafficking-related offenses leading to the prosecution of human traffickers and to promote public awareness.
d. Sexual Assault Unit - responsible for investigating and filing cases on sexually assaultive offenses that have victims aged 17 years and older.
(1) Sex Crime Cold Case/CODIS Hits Detail - investigate unsolved sex crime cases in response to Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) notifications.

e. Sex Offender Registration and Tracking (SORT) – responsible for sex offender registration; monitoring of registered sex offenders, and follow-up investigation on failure to register as sex offender offenses, and apprehension of sex offenders. TBP 7.31

3. Victim Assistance Section - process appropriate letters to victims of violent personal crimes; assist with Crime Victim Compensation applications; and conduct victim follow-up and refer to appropriate community resource.
B. The Criminal Investigations Support Division is responsible for

a. Commercial Auto Theft Unit - inspect, monitor and enforce the Transportation Code Chapter 501 and Occupations Code Chapter 2302 covering automotive salvage yards, repair shops, and body shops; target organized auto theft activities; investigate theft and unauthorized use of commercial motor vehicles, including commercial trailers, boats, and airplanes.

b. Crime Scene Search Unit - identify, collect, and process evidence of all homicides, suicides and other deaths under suspicious circumstances, sexual assaults, critical police incidents, visible bodily injury to a child fourteen (14) years of age or younger, visible bodily injury to a person sixty-five (65) years of age or older, visible bodily injury to a disabled person, and requests from on scene supervisor of the division concerned. The Crime Scene Search Unit may be requested for property crimes only when the collection of physical evidence exceeds patrol capabilities.

c. Digital Forensic Lab - responsible for providing technical assistance to investigators who are investigating computer-related offenses; forensically examine all seized phones, computers, media or other devices that may contain digital or electronic evidence in criminal or administrative cases; and assist other sections of the department in the investigation of computer-related offenses.

a. School Resource Unit (SRU) provides general police services for the school districts located within the city whose primary function is to create a safe environment in schools through efforts in crime prevention, intervention with students, and enforcement of the law.

b. Youth Services – act as a resource for procedures unique to handling cases involving children; provide a secure holding and interview area; administrate the First Offender Program; records retention/management of all filed cases involving child actors; liaison with Texas Juvenile Justice Department, Tarrant County Juvenile Services, Denton County Juvenile Services, and various school districts inside the city of Fort Worth. TBP 10.02
3. Jail Operations - the coordination of the jail operations. TBP 2.24

a. Jail Unit - is responsible for the intake of arrested individuals by the Fort Worth Police Department and the Fort Worth City Marshals, operating the central intake facility, acting as a liaison with Tarrant County Jail and contract service providers for jail services, and coordinating the transfer of custody or release of those arrested individuals.
b. Intoxilyzer Detail - the administering, recording, and processing of all intoxilyzer tests for individuals arrested on suspicion of driving while under the influence of alcohol.
C. Forensic Science Division - responsible for the scientific evaluation and testing of physical evidence and providing expert testimony on the test/evaluation results.

1. Biology Unit – evaluates evidence for the presence of biological material that can be used for testing, conducts DNA analyses and enters appropriate profiles into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS).

2. Chemistry Unit – conducts testing to identify controlled substances, non-controlled substances, plant materials, synthetic marijuana precursor chemicals, and other chemicals used in the manufacture of illegal drugs. The Chemistry Unit also conducts blood alcohol concentration (BAC) examinations.

3. Evidence Handling/Photography Unit – coordinates evidence viewings, outsources of examinations not performed by the Crime Laboratory, and receives and transports evidence between the Crime Laboratory, the Property Control Unit, and external agencies.

4. Firearms and Toolmark Unit – conducts the examination of all types of firearms and firearms-related evidence. This includes firearm functionality testing, microscopic examination and comparison of ammunition components such as bullets and cartridge cases, serial number restoration, non-firearm toolmark examinations and muzzle to target distance determinations. The Firearm Unit is also responsible for the entry of appropriate cartridge case evidence into the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN).

5. Latent Print Unit – develops latent prints from items of physical evidence, conducts comparative analyses of latent prints to known prints and enters appropriate prints into multiple Automated Fingerprint Identification Systems (AFIS) databases.
D. Warrant and Records Management Division

1. Police Records Management Section - process all citizen requests for police reports, from origination to archival of completed reports; process accident reports electronically and fill requests for accident reports; and process requests from law enforcement/other governmental agencies for records held by the department.

a. Police Record Management Center (PRMC) - oversee the records center for police department, both criminal and administrative; retain records in warehouse and database to ensure the timely retention schedules have been met; and assist the department liaisons on incoming and outgoing records.

b. Records Management System (RMS) - oversee and coordinate the security, training, updates, and daily usage of the RMS software to ensure timely processing of police reports and dissemination of information entered into the system.

c. Accident Report System - oversee and send out notices for electronic accident reporting corrections; review all accident reports entered into the system and send to Texas Department of Transportation (TX DOT); ensure that all accidents are reviewed and reported in by the ten (10) day deadline for certain grant funding (i.e. Commercial Motor Vehicle); communicate with officers’ chain of commands on rejected reports and reports not entered into the system; and communicate and be the liaison with TXDOT and Report Beam (software vendor) to address any issues with electronic reporting as well as provide and enter the security needed by department personnel to access the system.

2. Data Collection and Reporting Unit (DRU) - review and distribute all police reports entered into the Records Management System; process the reports of non-consent wrecker towing and repossessions within the corporate limits of the City of Fort Worth; and, process all dispatched calls and online reporting of offenses made by citizens as well as supplemental information for police reports.

a. National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) Unit - oversee and review all arrests for proper coding into the RMS system; oversee and review all offenses for proper NIBRS coding and data; review the NIBRS error log and correct data in RMS; report crime statistic data to Texas Department of Public Safety for the department.

3. Warrant and Identification Unit - maintain all departmental arrest fingerprint and criminal history records; assist with the identification of criminal offenders through fingerprint classification; maintain original warrant files and confirm Class B and above misdemeanor and all felony warrants; and maintain and confirm both protective order and emergency protective order files.
E. Property and Evidence Management Division

1. Vehicle Impound Unit - coordinate the impoundment, protection and preservation of vehicles in the custody of the department; manage the disposal of vehicles impounded and associated property through semi-monthly vehicle auctions; and, manage the lawful disposition of vehicles and associated property awarded to the department.
2. Property and Evidence Unit - coordinate the protection, preservation, storage and disposal of evidence and property in the custody of the department.
